answer: 'Person513,' says I, suddenly, 'were you ever married?' 'Lord, Master Person252,' replied Person513. 'What's put marriage in your head?' 'I don't know!--You mustn't marry more than one person at a time, may you, Person513?' 'Certainly not,' says Person513, with the promptest decision. 'But if you marry a person, and the person dies, why then you may marry another person, mayn't you, Person513?' 'YOU MAY,' says Person513, 'if you choose, my dear. That's a matter of opinion.' 'But what is your opinion, Person513?' said I. I asked her, and looked curiously at her, because she looked so curiously at me. 'My opinion is,' said Person513, taking her eyes from me, after a little indecision and going on with her work, 'that I never was married myself, Master Person252, and that I don't expect to be. That's all I know about the subject.' 'You an't cross, I suppose, Person513, are you?' 'No, my dear,' says Person513, giving me a good squeeze, because, being very plump, whenever she made any little exertion after she was dressed, some of the buttons on the back of her gown flew off. And I recollect two bursting to the opposite side of the parlour, while she was hugging me. 'Now let me hear some more about the Person418,' said Person513, who was not quite right in the name yet, 'for I an't heard half enough.'
